doc.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023

title: Staying out of the vocal; the unison approach
summary: Horns must not compete with the vocal; Quincy Jones advised blending into the rhythm track; unisons carry a line through heavy harmony.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: and make sure that they occur in their own space because I’m just the frosting on the cake.
Absolutely. That is one hundred percent right. If you’re playing when the vocal is playing the horns are not going to be heard because the vocal has to be heard.
Did anybody ever have to tell you that or did you just know it?

I guess it was a combination of listening to all of those top 40 records that I had to transcribe, and okay they’re kind of — the horns have their own thing. You know there’s a vocal and there’s the horn parts you know so it kind of got that. Then I went in with Quincy doing something sometime you know and we just kind of talked about kind of how to approach it. And he said, “Yeah, you want to stay away from the vocal and you want to try to become part of the rhythm track.” So obviously if the rhythm hits or whatever, or a melody line — instrumental melody line should be played you know you want to be kind of blend into the track like you were there from the beginning.
Tom also said an interesting thing that you were basically the “King of the Unisons” which I thought was interesting.

With horn parts when you have a lot of voicing and you have a lot of movement you can — I try to think of the horn parts as a melody. And when you have a lot of harmony and they’re not going to be — it’s not like a big band where the horns are going to be featured and you’re going to hear all of the parts and everything, they’re going to put the horns down a little bit and the melody part that I write for horns can get lost with all of the harmony. So if there’s a line that you want to kind of emphasize and make sure everybody remembers, unison will come through better than a harmonized part.
